# V1 implementation and stacked-PR execution

Status: active execution portfolio. Baseline: `origin/main` at `0a971b211` (#172); the work branch carries local T01/T11 commits `20ce30cd1`, `a37025927` and `f4ce5f22d`, with earlier documentation reconciliation preserved in the dirty worktree. [Task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [findings](V1-FINDINGS.md), [roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Execution status: the branch contains T01 producer/consumer and unchanged-applied-head commits (`20ce30cd1`, `f4ce5f22d`) and the independent T11 installer commit (`a37025927`). T02, T03, T03-PRE, T03-HISTORY, T04, T04-PNPM, T04-LOCK, T05, T10-BINS and T10-AUTH remain implemented in the worktree. On 2026-09-28, all 1,861 Nextest tests passed and line coverage reached 93.44%; the aggregate `just ci` recipe still exits at the sandbox-protected cargo-deny advisory lock, while the offline audit passes with authorized cache access. Docs, workflow contracts, zizmor, release behavior and the 90% coverage gate also pass individually. The owner-approved T05 policy is fail-closed E121 with manual recovery guidance; no automatic deletion or persisted checkpoint is added. The local `pr/v1-current-contract` pointer exists, but no PR has been opened remotely. Architectural D01 choices, remote delivery and publication remain separate decisions.

## PR-sized lanes and current position

| Lane | PR-sized units | Dependency or constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release/wire | T01 producer/consumer fix → T02 schema repair → T03 contextual decisions → T03-PRE baselines; T03-HISTORY inherited/root verification follows T03 and T04 | T01 fix is committed; other units local; stack separation remains |
| Native resolution | T04 manifest-local names → T04-PNPM protocols → T04-LOCK refresh | Implemented locally; review corrections closed; stack separation remains |
| Installer | T11 version/source fidelity | Committed locally as `a37025927`; independent review and combined full CI pass |
| Early workflows | T10-BINS binary inventory/unsupported builders → T10-AUTH native auth | Both implemented locally; docs preserve owner-controlled native hooks, which retain their normal environment |
| Apply recovery join | T05 input retention and partial-run detection | Core changes, regression coverage and manual recovery guidance are implemented. The owner chose fail-closed E121 over auto-deletion or a persisted checkpoint; if stable exit output is staged but `git rm --cached pre.json` fails, the retained file requires the documented manual recovery path. |

T01 is the v0.9 release-path priority. Its merge permits the bot to regenerate the release PR; fresh decision/source agreement and passing CI must precede any separately authorized merge/publication. Other lanes do not automatically become v0.9 release requirements. Existing-contract fixes can run while the architectural decisions below are being reviewed.

## Architectural stack after D01

| Stack | Order | What each boundary proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity/authority | T06 canonical references → T06-HISTORY historic ownership; T07 native/Maturin authority follows T06 | One resolver across authored/generated consumers; no transferred or regressed release history; native metadata agrees with planned versions |
| Effects/retry | T08 shared physical effects → T08-RETRY tagged-candidate completion | One owner per irreversible effect; required publications gate announcements; local retry does not lose push/forge work |
| Python completion | T09 required file-set recovery → T09-ROUTES read/upload destinations | Complete declared files, not first-file presence; no changed bytes or untrusted destination on retry |
| Workflow integration | T10 intent-selected outputs | Builds follow the verified release intent; package-owner lifecycle hooks retain native behavior and remain outside Callisto's operation graph |
| Evidence | T12 production matrix → T12-DX measured onboarding | Executed/skipped/simulated evidence distinguished; first-release setup and credentials included in timing |

T06-HISTORY → T07 is a true stack: historical and native-authority changes share model/graph consumers. T08 follows both; T08-RETRY → T09 is also serialized because both change local/CLI release entry boundaries. Independent read-only review and native fixture drafting can run alongside those implementation units once their interfaces are fixed; competing edits cannot. T09-ROUTES follows T09 because both own the registry adapter. JSON task dependencies are authoritative; stack grouping is not permission to ignore a dependency.

## D01: approved directions and remaining model choices

The owner approved Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as current scope, architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet, canonical-only new exact references, registry publication before shared tags/public announcements, and package-owner control of native lifecycle hooks. Remaining wire shapes and migration rules below are proposals, not hidden release gates.

| Contract | Proposed bounded choice | Approval/evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical references | The owner chose canonical slash-qualified IDs for every new exact reference; reject new bare and colon-form aliases, and read existing forms only through an explicit ownership migration boundary | Specify which historical records remain readable and how migration is surfaced; cover config, groups, changesets, pre-state and reports |
| Owner identity | Reuse a stable source-directory locator plus its explicit canonical distribution roster; do not introduce an opaque globally persistent ID | Choose a durable owner field versus deterministic derivation from the retained source snapshot; specify rename/move refusal or explicit mapping |
| Tag migration | Do not rename existing tags; retain observed legacy templates/history and select one deterministic template for new releases | Settle independent/fixed defaults with owner identity; do not add a second inference-based tag authority |
| Wire compatibility | Preserve existing string versions where context suffices; version documents whose owner/effect/output semantics change | Enumerate decision/intent/manifest/envelope/receipt readers, accepted old versions, stale decisions and old-intent rerun support; reject unsupported migration explicitly |
| Conflicting pre-state aliases | A legacy bare key may resolve to an owner that already has a canonical key in the same file | Choose behavior when both keys carry different versions; current `or_insert` keeps the canonical value and silently drops the migrated legacy value |
| Maturin | First support Cargo-owned `dynamic = ["version"]` and inherited Cargo authority with native Python mapping | Specify static co-located metadata behavior, precedence, unsupported mappings/backends and built wheel/sdist checks; do not force equal numeric strings into one grammar |
| Announcement | The owner chose required Cargo/npm/PyPI publications before a shared tag and public GitHub release; a future Go source tag can itself be a publication | Specify draft creation and upload ordering and prove all required owner outputs complete before public announcement |
| Registry file set | Declare selected outputs before build; bind exact trusted filenames/digests after build without mutating sealed intent | Choose per-file effects or an aggregate operation with explicit partial-state proof; define how build inventory is covered by the existing envelope and how local retries retain original bytes |
| Python destinations | Separate credential-free index/read and upload routing; public PyPI/TestPyPI first | Choose support versus explicit refusal for custom, authenticated and HTML-only indexes; Twine credentials do not authenticate observation automatically |
| Native lifecycle hooks | Package owners control hook scripts and any effects they initiate; Callisto preserves native behavior and does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks | Settled owner boundary: preserve it in future publisher changes; do not require hook migration or promise that external hook effects are coordinated |

D01 records testable contracts in the proposed architecture/ADR and PR packets. Area specs remain current-behavior documents: amend them on each implementation branch with the behavior, and review/hash-bind that contract before a gated implementation handoff. ADR 12 stays proposed until owner acceptance and the implementing merge. No single approved future delta spec currently exists, so the portfolio JSON intentionally has no `linked_spec` or fabricated `spec_hash`; affected criterion mappings are not coverage of all 220 existing criteria.

## Stack mechanics without new infrastructure

Use ordinary Git branches/worktrees and the existing PR workflow. No stack tool was found in the inspected repository configuration; do not require a new tool to execute this plan.

          if-no-files-found: error

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]
    # Artifact-less sources skip build; a failed or cancelled build must still block.
    # !cancelled() not always(): a status function still defeats the skipped-ancestor
    # rule, but cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'false' || needs.build.result == 'success')
    timeout-minutes: 60
    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The release-source checkout alone needs Git credentials because
          # graph-owned tag dispatch pushes from this repository.
          persist-credentials: true
      # Downloaded outside the workspace (under $RUNNER_TEMP, like
      # setup-callisto's own binary install): callisto release execute
      # re-checks release trust before every dispatch, which requires a
      # worktree with no tracked or untracked files -- landing these inside
      # the checkout would dirty it and fail that check before anything
      # gets published.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        env:
          HAS_ARTIFACTS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          (cd "$intent_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          if [[ "$HAS_ARTIFACTS" == true ]]; then
            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          fi
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$receipt_dir"
          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$build_dir/release-artifacts")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
"}}

# Scoped polyglot release model

Status: proposed v1 design, not current behavior. Owner scope: Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI now; leave room for Go and .NET/NuGet without implementing their publishers. Current contracts remain in [the specs](../specs/INDEX.md). Work is sequenced in [the roadmap](../projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md) and [the plan](../projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json).

## Four concepts

| Concept | Responsibility | Not equivalent to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release owner | Source/version authority and the outputs released together | A display name or registry destination |
| Distribution | Canonical ecosystem-qualified identity and native package name | A source directory or import/module name |
| Version authority | Literal or supported inherited/derived source, plus each distribution's native representation | A grammar guessed from a JSON string |
| Release effect | One required external effect, its destination, evidence and prerequisites | A package tag proving all publications finished |

Keep existing types where they already express these responsibilities. A `PackageKey` locates a directory; it does not prove identity survives a directory move. Do not add opaque IDs or a public plugin protocol without a demonstrated need. The release-owner representation and wire migration must be specified before implementation.

## Canonical references and migration

- New exact inputs, generated config, changesets and machine reports use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; new bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names.
- Short labels may remain in human output, but never become an alternate identity authority. Ecosystem-specific native names stay available for manifest rewrites and publisher arguments.
- Existing bare/colon references are migration inputs only, not alternate spellings for new identities. Resolve them only through established ownership; ambiguous input fails with an actionable diagnostic. Specify historical-reader and schema-version support before changing persisted formats.
- Adding or removing a same-named sibling, adding a canonical manifest or changing the primary manifest must not transfer another owner's history or regress the last release. A genuine rename/move needs a declared migration boundary, not guessing from current path existence.
- Keep [ADR 11](../adr/0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) in force until [the proposed replacement](../adr/0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) is implemented and accepted. Do not rename existing tags merely to canonicalize selectors.

## Native versions and dependencies

A release owner can have several distribution outputs. Shared versioning is deliberate; co-location or a build dependency alone does not require version coupling. The initial supported derived-version case is Maturin's Cargo-owned Python version. Preserve `dynamic = ["version"]`, use the known SemVer-to-PEP-440 mapping and verify the built metadata. Do not introduce a universal reversible version converter; unsupported mappings and arbitrary SCM-derived backends need an explicit support decision.

Reuse the native dependency graph and derived release-operation DAG. Preserve each edge's manifest, declared key/alias, resolved distribution, constraint and dependency kind. A native Cargo edge must not become a dependency on every distribution produced by the same source package.

- Native registry dependency: update that ecosystem's reference and derive only relevant publication prerequisites. Range coverage, version cascade and publication order are distinct decisions.
- Embedded/build input: the consuming artifact needs those bytes or sources. It does not necessarily need that input published to Cargo, npm or PyPI. Builders and CI retain build ordering; add explicit cross-project input relationships only for a supported concrete case.
- Version coupling: retain fixed/linked policies separately from dependency edges; do not infer a major bump of every wrapper from an internal-language change.
- Runtime services and arbitrary cross-language discovery are outside the release graph's scope.

For pnpm, retain the difference between `workspace:*`, explicit workspace ranges, aliases, relative paths and catalogs. Let pnpm perform pack-time transformations. For Python, preserve extras, markers and native specifiers; document direct-URL and dynamic-backend support rather than treating them as ordinary ranges. Cargo inherited versions/dependencies require their authoritative root paths in both live and historical reads.

## Effects and completion

For current registry ecosystems, the proposed default is required registry publications confirmed before a shared tag and public GitHub announcement. A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.

Within Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.

A retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.

PyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.

Registry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.

## Future compatibility examples

- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.
- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.
- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.

These are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.

## Prior art and research limits

| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |
| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |
| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |
| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |

Sources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).

Competitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Non-goals

No universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.

# V1 system findings

Baseline: main `8ef9aa5a4` (#168), audited on 2026-09-26. This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec. Corrections implemented locally are labeled and remain unshipped until merged. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. The earlier isolated run passed 6 identity, 5 schema-guard, 10 release-command and 14 durable-release tests. Those tests do not establish the missing producer/consumer or ecosystem coverage. No full `just ci`, hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run was performed in that audit.

## Implemented locally, awaiting merge

These corrections are not shipped. [Batch verification](V1-VERIFICATION.md) records local results and remaining checks.

| Finding | Correction and evidence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-ENV | Unchanged decide stdout reproduced E281 at the baseline. The CLI accepts the decide report or strict bare wire while preserving typed validation. Review also found strict post-move verification rejected the action's own update with E148; the model now permits only that exact applied-head transition. Real-binary, model and shell action tests cover the boundaries and unrelated-change negatives. | T01 | REL-PR-02, REL-PR-04, REL-PR-07 |
| SYS-INSTALL | Auto installation honors explicit/action-ref versions, including inside Callisto source. Local compilation requires explicit source selection and native workspace ownership checks. Isolated installer fixtures cover consumer names, pins, source rejection and attestation/fallback behavior. | T11 | REL-PR-06 |
| SYS-SCHEMA | Custom string serializers now have string-shaped, named schema definitions. A full JSON Schema validator checks every exposed schema target against real report/durable payloads and malformed nested values; full CI passes. | T02 | CLI-SCHEMA-01, CLI-OUT-05, REL-CMD-12 |
| SYS-PYDEC | Durable release entries, operations, slots and bound registry observations decode versions with the owning distribution's grammar. Genuine Python stable release plan/execute/rerun tests preserve PEP 440 values and reject foreign rosters; independent review found no must-fix. | T03 | REL-AUTH-01/03 |
| SYS-CASCADE | Dependency declarations now retain both local key and native target; graph walking and shared cascade/floor/snapshot rewriting use the declaration's manifest ecosystem. Cargo aliases, inherited root declarations, promoted dual Cargo/npm packages and normalized Python graph names have regressions; independent review cleared T04 and full CI passes. | T04 | VER-CAS-07, VER-PRE-09 |
| SYS-PYPRE | Pre-release baselines now resolve their historical/display identity before native grammar validation. Validation uses the original JSON spelling, so PEP 440 fallback cannot normalize invalid SemVer input; Python stable cycles, promoted/historical keys, malformed values, exit and resume are covered. | T03-PRE | VER-PRE-01/03/06/10 |
| SYS-INHERITED, SYS-ROOT | Historical release verification now reads effective versions from Git blobs, including Cargo workspace inheritance; normalized root/member/changelog paths are checked against the claimed roster. Tests cover authority-only root changes, unclaimed owners and unsafe paths. | T03-HISTORY | REL-AUTH-02, VER-APPLY-13 |
| SYS-PNPM | Dependency state now retains pnpm workspace suffixes, alias targets and relative paths. Explicit SemVer ranges are checked and safely rewritten; aliases preserve keys, relative references resolve only to admitted members, and native pack/frozen-install tests cover version and snapshot flows. | T04-PNPM | WS-ID-10, VER-CAS-05/06 |
| SYS-LOCK | Lockfile refresh and staging now include every actual version/dependency/platform/optional-dependency write ecosystem, including dual manifests and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cross-ecosystem and dependency-only regressions pass in full CI. | T04-LOCK | VER-APPLY-14, VER-PRE-08 |
| SYS-VERSION-RECOVERY | Consumed changesets and pre-state deletions are deferred until lock refresh and generated-state staging succeed. Partial-run detection checks staged effective versions, permits metadata-only edits and handles the examined prerelease exit and inherited-Cargo cases; regressions cover untracked inputs, failed deletion staging, staged/restored versions, exit-state stable bumps, and a fresh E121 refusal after pre-state deletion staging fails. | T05 | VER-APPLY-08/10/13/15/16 |
| SYS-BINS, SYS-NONCARGO | Cargo executable discovery covers explicit and automatic bin targets. npm/Python executables are rejected as unsupported generated artifact builders before writes, while registry-only setup remains available. Focused init and manifest tests plus full CI pass. | T10-BINS | CLI-INIT-01/02/12, CLI-WF-04 |
| SYS-AUTH | Generated release actions configure npm auth in a mode-0600 temporary user config using `${NPM_TOKEN}` interpolation (the secret is not written to disk), map PyPI credentials to Twine, support Bun's token contract, and filter release credentials including `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from Python build subprocesses. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain normal package-owner-defined behavior; Callisto does not suppress or rewrite them. Fake-tool and environment-filter tests pass; generated workflow tests keep secrets out of version-pr/plan/build. | T10-AUTH | CLI-WF-03/04; ADR 4 |

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-OWNER | `sole_owner_at`: current first-manifest path existence is not historic name/full-roster ownership. Reproduced loss of a bare tag after sibling rename or addition of a new primary canonical manifest. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-DEMOTION | `tags.rs`: removing a same-named sibling loses a newer qualified tag and chooses an older bare release. Reproduced; inference can replay already-released work. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-RETRY | `derive_unreleased_decision`: local tags exclude a package before remaining operations are observed. Reproduced tag creation followed by push failure, then exit 0 with `Nothing to release.` and no receipt. Generated simple CI uses this path; Callisto's own committed-roster CI does not. | T08-RETRY | REL-RERUN-02; REL-CMD-01/08 need coordinated selection changes |
| SYS-BARRIER | `release/derive.rs`: a dual Cargo/npm owner creates a shared physical tag/GitHub publication after one distribution but before the other's publish. Reproduced plan ordering; per-distribution gates do not enforce the owner's completion barrier. | T08 | REL-ORD-01 |
| SYS-NAPI | `commands/init.rs`: generated native builds and placement use workspace-wide napi selection rather than the verified intent. An unrelated addon can block a Cargo-only release. Source-confirmed. | T10 | CLI-WF-04; committed roster authority |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |
| SYS-PYFILES | `provider/registry.rs` returns Exact for any matching non-yanked Python file; `provider/mod.rs` adopts it as AlreadySatisfied. `registry_argv.rs` builds both wheel and sdist. Source-confirmed partial-upload retry gap; no live fault-injection run yet. | T09 | REL-PUB-04/08, REL-RERUN-01/04 |
| SYS-PYROUTES | `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload. Source-confirmed single-route assumption; servers with distinct read/upload routes cannot generally use one override. Public defaults use separate native routes. | T09-ROUTES | REL-PUB-04/08; private-index policy |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Status changeset attribution and well-formedness checks still scan display ids through `PackageId::resolve_unique`, while version aggregation uses `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`. Source-visible resolver divergence can reject a valid secondary native name or accept an unrelated qualified selector. Add a paired status/version fixture and migrate both status helpers with the other selector consumers (T06).
- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes, complete Python files or the desired npm dist-tag. Artifact-set completion is a correctness fix (T09); universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- PyPI yanking is per file. The current classifier treats any matching yanked file as Absent even alongside non-yanked files. A yank is not deletion or permission to overwrite; confirm conflict/partial semantics with the required-output model (T09).
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).

## gh attestation verify
    
    `gh attestation verify [<file-path> | oci://<image-uri>] [--owner | --repo] [flags]
    `

Verify the integrity and provenance of an artifact using its associated cryptographically signed attestations.

## Understanding Verification

An attestation is a claim (i.e. a provenance statement) made by an actor (i.e. a GitHub Actions workflow) regarding a subject (i.e. an artifact).

In order to verify an attestation, you must provide an artifact and validate:

  * the identity of the actor that produced the attestation
  * the expected attestation predicate type (the nature of the claim)

By default, this command enforces the `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1` predicate type. To verify other attestation predicate types use the `--predicate-type` flag.

The "actor identity" consists of:

  * the repository or the repository owner the artifact is linked with
  * the Actions workflow that produced the attestation (a.k.a the signer workflow)

This identity is then validated against the attestation's certificate's SourceRepository, SourceRepositoryOwner, and SubjectAlternativeName (SAN) fields, among others.

It is up to you to decide how precisely you want to enforce this identity.

At a minimum, this command requires either:

  * the `--owner` flag (e.g. --owner github), or
  * the `--repo` flag (e.g. --repo github/example)

The more precisely you specify the identity, the more control you will have over the security guarantees offered by the verification process.

Ideally, the path of the signer workflow is also validated using the `--signer-workflow` or `--cert-identity` flags.

Please note: if your attestation was generated via a reusable workflow then that reusable workflow is the signer whose identity needs to be validated. In this situation, you must use either the `--signer-workflow` or the `--signer-repo` flag.

For more options, see the other available flags.

## Loading Artifacts And Attestations

To specify the artifact, this command requires:

  * a file path to an artifact, or
  * a container image URI (e.g. `oci://<image-uri>`)
    * (note that if you provide an OCI URL, you must already be authenticated with its container registry)

By default, this command will attempt to fetch relevant attestations via the GitHub API using the values provided to `--owner` or `--repo`.

To instead fetch attestations from your artifact's OCI registry, use the `--bundle-from-oci` flag.

For offline verification using attestations stored on disk (c.f. the download command) provide a path to the `--bundle` flag.

## Additional Policy Enforcement

Given the `--format=json` flag, upon successful verification this command will output a JSON array containing one entry per verified attestation.

This output can then be used for additional policy enforcement, i.e. by being piped into a policy engine.

Each object in the array contains two properties:

  * an `attestation` object, which contains the bundle that was verified
  * a `verificationResult` object, which is a parsed representation of the contents of the bundle that was verified.

Within the `verificationResult` object you will find:

  * `signature.certificate`, which is a parsed representation of the X.509 certificate embedded in the attestation,
`--signer-workflow <string>`
    Enforce that the workflow that signed the attestation matches the provided value ([host/]<owner>/<repo>/<path>/<to>/<workflow>)
`--source-digest <string>`
    Enforce that the digest associated with the source repository matches the provided value
`--source-ref <string>`
    Enforce that the git ref associated with the source repository matches the provided value
`-t`, `--template <string>`
    Format JSON output using a Go template; see "gh help formatting"

### Examples

    $ gh attestation verify example.bin --repo github/example
    
    # Verify an artifact linked with an organization

    # Verify an artifact and output the full verification result

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs or builds the Callisto binary. Factored out of action.yml so
# callisto-action's own environment setup can call it directly by path
# (github.action_path has no ref-ambiguous `uses:` to resolve), instead of
# duplicating this logic.
set -euo pipefail

# Install into $RUNNER_TEMP so the binary never lands inside the workspace
# tree (preventing accidental git-staging by downstream steps that run
# "git add -A").
CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
mkdir -p "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
TAG_NAME="$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"
SOURCE="$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE"

if [[ "$SOURCE" != "auto" && "$SOURCE" != "local" ]]; then
  echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto source '$SOURCE' (expected auto or local)"
  exit 1
fi

# With no explicit version override, install the release this action's own
# invocation is pinned to (GITHUB_ACTION_REF, github.action_ref) rather than
# whatever is newest, so `callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@X.Y.Z` always
# installs X.Y.Z. Falls back to true "latest" when the ref is unset (local or
# unpinned invocation) or matches no published callisto@ tag.
if [[ "$SOURCE" == "auto" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" && -n "${GITHUB_ACTION_REF:-}" ]]; then
  resolved_tag=$(git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git 'callisto@*' 2>/dev/null \
    | awk -v ref="$GITHUB_ACTION_REF" '$1 == ref { print $2 }' \
    | sed -e 's#^refs/tags/##' -e 's/\^{}$//' \
    | sort -V | tail -n1) || true
  if [[ -n "$resolved_tag" ]]; then
    echo "Resolved action ref $GITHUB_ACTION_REF to $resolved_tag"
    TAG_NAME="$resolved_tag"
  fi
fi

# Validate verification mode
VERIFICATION="${INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION:-fallback}"
case "$VERIFICATION" in
  require|fallback|skip) ;;
  *)
    echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto verification '$VERIFICATION' (valid values: require, fallback, skip)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# Detect OS platform architecture for pre-built binaries
OS_NAME=$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
ARCH_NAME=$(uname -m)

if [[ "$OS_NAME" == "darwin" ]]; then
  if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "arm64" ]]; then
    ASSET_NAME="callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
  else
    ASSET_NAME=""
  fi
elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == "linux" ]]; then
  if [[ "$ARCH_NAME" == "x86_64" ]]; then
    ASSET_NAME="callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz"
  else
    ASSET_NAME=""
  fi
elif [[ "$OS_NAME" == *"mingw"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"msys"* || "$OS_NAME" == *"windows"* ]]; then
  ASSET_NAME=""
else
  ASSET_NAME=""
fi

if [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" && "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" ]]; then
  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/latest/download/$ASSET_NAME"
elif [[ -n "$ASSET_NAME" ]]; then
  DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/$TAG_NAME/$ASSET_NAME"
fi

# Derive a crates.io version spec from TAG_NAME: "latest" installs
# whatever crates.io resolves as latest (no --version flag); an
# explicit tag ("callisto@0.5.0" or legacy "callisto-cli@0.5.0")
# strips either prefix down to the bare semver cargo install expects.
CRATE_VERSION="${TAG_NAME#callisto@}"; CRATE_VERSION="${CRATE_VERSION#callisto-cli@}"

# Pick a download destination whose extension matches ASSET_NAME
# (under $RUNNER_TEMP, never the workspace) so the extraction step
# below always has an archive it can actually open -- a hardcoded
# ".tar.gz" path here previously masked the fact that Windows assets
# are zip files, since tar -xzf can't read a zip regardless of what
# the file on disk is really named.
case "$ASSET_NAME" in
  *.zip)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.zip"
    ;;
  *.tar.gz)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    ;;
  *)
    DOWNLOAD_DEST="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto.tar.gz"
    ;;
esac

# A prebuilt asset runs with the job's privileges, so it must carry a
# GitHub attestation from the Callisto release workflow before it is
# extracted. require aborts on failure; fallback discards the asset and
# returns 1 so the crates.io path runs; skip trusts the asset.
verify_asset() {
  local reason=""
  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "skip" ]]; then
    echo "::warning::verification=skip: $ASSET_NAME was not verified"
    return 0
  fi
  if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    reason="gh is not installed"
  elif ! gh attestation verify "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" \
      --repo orin-dx/callisto \
      --signer-workflow orin-dx/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml \
      --deny-self-hosted-runners; then
    reason="attestation verification failed"
  fi
  [[ -z "$reason" ]] && return 0
  rm -f "$DOWNLOAD_DEST"
  if [[ "$VERIFICATION" == "require" ]]; then
    echo "::error::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason (verification=require)"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "::warning::cannot verify $ASSET_NAME: $reason; discarding it and installing from crates.io (verification=fallback)"
  return 1
}

# Download, verify and extract the prebuilt asset; nonzero means use the fallback chain.
fetch_prebuilt() {
  curl -sL -f "$DOWNLOAD_URL" -o "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  verify_asset || return 1
  # Extract only the expected binary, never the whole archive.
  case "$ASSET_NAME" in
    *.zip)
      unzip -q "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" callisto.exe -d "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
      ;;
    *)
      tar -xzf "$DOWNLOAD_DEST" -C "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR" callisto
      ;;
  esac
}

# Dependencies named callisto-cli do not establish checkout source ownership.
owns_local_source() {
  local workspace git_root metadata
  workspace=$(cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && pwd -P) || return 1
  git_root=$(git -C "$workspace" rev-parse --show-toplevel) || return 1
  [[ "$git_root" == "$workspace" ]] || return 1

## Assessment

Claude identified real failure modes, but the recommendations are at different levels of readiness. **W1 is a useful CI check with a narrower claim than stated. W3 and D01 need a defined authority and migration contract before implementation. W4 addresses a real leak risk but must cover output paths beyond receipts. W10 contains one concrete identity bug and one policy choice.**

### 1. W1 — release attestation check

**Verdict: do it, but specify the asset and what the check proves.** A job with `contents: read` and `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` fits the existing CI workflow and keeps registry credentials out. The installer already passes that token and verifies the downloaded asset against the release workflow’s signer identity in [install-callisto.sh](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto/scripts/install-callisto.sh:101).

Two claims need correction:

- Fork PRs do receive a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`; they do not receive repository secrets. Restricting this job to same-repo PRs may still be sensible for cost or policy, but “fork PRs get no token” is false. [GitHub’s event documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows) states the read-only behavior.
- `gh release download` without a tag selects the *latest* release and requires an asset pattern. The job must name the expected platform asset and verify it with `--repo` and `--signer-workflow`. It will test the currently selected release and CI token access, not prove every historical release or the full installer fallback path. [GitHub CLI download](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_download) and [attestation verification](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify) document those boundaries.

I would run the job on main pushes and same-repo PRs as proposed, then record an intentional behavior for a repository with no suitable release. The release-workflow policy script can stay untouched; the CI workflow contract checks should still be run.

### 2. W3 — Python partial uploads

**Verdict: correct completion rule, incomplete execution design.** The defect is supported: one matching non-yanked file currently yields `Exact` in [registry.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs:574), while the publisher builds a wheel and sdist and uploads a broad glob in [registry_argv.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs:334).

“Every file the build produced” raises the decisive question: **which build, and where is its trusted inventory retained for a retry?** The current publisher rebuilds inside the effect, then uploads from `dist/`. It does not bind that output set and its hashes to the sealed release intent. Rebuilding after a partial upload could produce different bytes; observing the new build as the required set would silently change the release target. The current `dist/` glob also does not itself prove that every selected file came from this invocation.

The safe sequence is to declare selected outputs, build into an isolated location, record exact filenames and hashes in a trusted artifact inventory bound to the run, then observe each required file before selecting only missing files for upload. A yanked required file or mismatched hash should block. The plan must define local retry retention and index lag behavior. Its comparison to tags/assets is directionally useful, but [REL-RERUN-03](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/specs/release.json:245) does not already specify Python file-set proof.

### 3. W4 — redacted provider output

**Verdict: prefer closed structured details, but scope the leak paths first.** Claude’s correction is sound: `redact_native_output` does not exist, and [redact_known_secrets](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/registry.rs:114) can only replace secrets it knows. A closed enum for persisted diagnostic details removes free-text credential exposure from that field.

There is an important scope distinction: provider **observations are already closed enums** in [release_observation.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release_observation.rs:80). Free-text error fields and subprocess stderr remain elsewhere, and the CLI runner can print redacted native output. Changing a receipt detail type alone would not establish “nothing can leak by construction.” Inventory every path from provider stdout/stderr into errors, live logs, summaries and persisted files; use closed data wherever Callisto owns the diagnostic. Keep native stderr handling as a separate, explicitly limited boundary.

The proposed enum also needs enough fixed cases to distinguish an authentication failure from a transport failure or malformed response without accidentally reporting either as an absent remote object.

### 4. W10 — target declarations and Python dev groups

**Target declarations: accept the defect, challenge the size estimate.** [RewriteKey](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/cascade.rs:576) distinguishes manifest, name and dependency kind, but no target table. Cargo extraction and rewriting currently walk top-level dependency sections in [cargo.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:398). A discriminator on `RewriteKey` alone cannot recover target declarations that were never emitted as edges, nor can the existing writer address their table. The fix needs a declaration locator carried through extraction, graph edges, cascade, snapshot and the format-preserving writer. Review public constructors and `check-api` together. This is a justified correction, but it is not merely one added key field.

**Python dev groups: defer the “yes” pending an owner choice.** [python.rs](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:459) reads published runtime dependencies and Poetry dependencies, but no dev groups. Cargo’s existing rule rewrites dev constraints without bumping the dependent; that is a plausible policy for Python groups, not evidence that users expect every local tooling group to participate in release versioning. Define which group formats are supported, how includes and duplicate declarations work, and whether stale pins are release errors before making this a gate.

### 5. D01 — owner contract

**Conflicting pre-state aliases: accept, and the merge site is confirmed.** [assign_promoted_pre_keys](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs:275) resolves keys, removes a legacy key and calls `entry(owner_key).or_insert(version)` at line 338. If the canonical key already exists, its value wins silently. A typed conflict naming both keys and original versions is appropriate. The check should occur before removal or mutation. Equal values can safely coalesce if that is stated explicitly.

**Owner identity: reject this as a settled recommendation.** The proposed architecture itself says a directory locator does not prove identity across moves in [polyglot-v1.md](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md:17). Deterministic derivation from a retained snapshot can identify an owner *within that snapshot*, but it does not by itself join old tags, decisions and pre-state records to the owner after a rename, move, new canonical manifest or roster change. “Refuse renames until explicit mapping exists” is safe only if the code can reliably detect those changes rather than treating them as a new owner. Specify the historical join key, the evidence used to detect uncertain transfer, and the mapping format before choosing persisted versus derived identity. This is the main unresolved D01 decision.

**Wire compatibility: accept the principle, require a document-by-document matrix.** A version bump should follow semantic change, and unsupported versions should fail explicitly. But [ReleaseDecisionV1](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs:627) already writes schema 2 while reading 1 and 2; other release documents have separate version gates and digests. Decide accepted old versions, whether old intents may be rerun, and how nested decision/snapshot versions are validated for each wire. “Bump only when meaning changes” is too broad to implement safely without that table.

## Recommended order

Start W1 with a focused downloaded-asset check. In parallel, settle D01’s historical owner join and wire reader matrix; those decisions unblock W8/W9. Specify W3’s trusted build inventory and retry retention before changing its classifier. Treat W4 as a diagnostic-path audit followed by targeted closed types. Split W10 into the target-declaration correctness fix and a separate owner decision on Python dev groups.

This is a source review, not execution evidence: I did not run CI, a live registry fault injection, or a hosted release.

**Conflicting pre-state aliases: accept, and the merge site is confirmed.** [assign_promoted_pre_keys](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs:275) resolves keys, removes a legacy key and calls `entry(owner_key).or_insert(version)` at line 338. If the canonical key already exists, its value wins silently. A typed conflict naming both keys and original versions is appropriate. The check should occur before removal or mutation. Equal values can safely coalesce if that is stated explicitly.

**Owner identity: reject this as a settled recommendation.** The proposed architecture itself says a directory locator does not prove identity across moves in [polyglot-v1.md](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md:17). Deterministic derivation from a retained snapshot can identify an owner *within that snapshot*, but it does not by itself join old tags, decisions and pre-state records to the owner after a rename, move, new canonical manifest or roster change. “Refuse renames until explicit mapping exists” is safe only if the code can reliably detect those changes rather than treating them as a new owner. Specify the historical join key, the evidence used to detect uncertain transfer, and the mapping format before choosing persisted versus derived identity. This is the main unresolved D01 decision.

**Wire compatibility: accept the principle, require a document-by-document matrix.** A version bump should follow semantic change, and unsupported versions should fail explicitly. But [ReleaseDecisionV1](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs:627) already writes schema 2 while reading 1 and 2; other release documents have separate version gates and digests. Decide accepted old versions, whether old intents may be rerun, and how nested decision/snapshot versions are validated for each wire. “Bump only when meaning changes” is too broad to implement safely without that table.

## Recommended order

Start W1 with a focused downloaded-asset check. In parallel, settle D01’s historical owner join and wire reader matrix; those decisions unblock W8/W9. Specify W3’s trusted build inventory and retry retention before changing its classifier. Treat W4 as a diagnostic-path audit followed by targeted closed types. Split W10 into the target-declaration correctness fix and a separate owner decision on Python dev groups.

This is a source review, not execution evidence: I did not run CI, a live registry fault injection, or a hosted release.

# Dependency Groups¶

This specification defines dependency groups, a mechanism for storing package requirements in `pyproject.toml` files such that they are not included in project metadata when it is built.

Dependency groups are suitable for internal development use-cases like linting and testing, as well as for projects which are not built for distribution, like collections of related scripts.

Fundamentally, dependency groups should be thought of as being a standardized subset of the capabilities of `requirements.txt` files (which are `pip`-specific).

## Specification¶

### Examples¶

This is a simple table which shows `docs` and `test` groups:
    
    [dependency-groups]
    docs = ["sphinx"]
    test = ["pytest>7", "coverage"]
    

and a similar table which defines `docs`, `test`, and `coverage` groups:
    
    [dependency-groups]
    docs = ["sphinx"]
    coverage = ["coverage[toml]"]
    test = ["pytest>7", {include-group = "coverage"}]
    

### The `[dependency-groups]` Table¶

Dependency groups are defined as a table in `pyproject.toml` named `dependency-groups`. The `dependency-groups` table contains an arbitrary number of user-defined keys, each of which has, as its value, a list of requirements.

`[dependency-groups]` keys, sometimes also called “group names”, must be valid non-normalized names. Tools which handle Dependency Groups MUST normalize these names before comparisons.

Tools SHOULD prefer to present the original, non-normalized name to users, and if duplicate names are detected after normalization, tools SHOULD emit an error.

Requirement lists, the values in `[dependency-groups]`, may contain strings, tables (`dict` in Python), or a mix of strings and tables. Strings must be valid dependency specifiers, and tables must be valid Dependency Group Includes.

### Dependency Group Include¶

A Dependency Group Include includes another Dependency Group in the current group.

An include is a table with exactly one key, `"include-group"`, whose value is a string, the name of another Dependency Group.

Includes are defined to be exactly equivalent to the contents of the named Dependency Group, inserted into the current group at the location of the include. For example, if `foo = ["a", "b"]` is one group, and `bar = ["c", {include-group = "foo"}, "d"]` is another, then `bar` should evaluate to `["c", "a", "b", "d"]` when Dependency Group Includes are expanded.

Dependency Group Includes may specify the same package multiple times. Tools SHOULD NOT deduplicate or otherwise alter the list contents produced by the include. For example, given the following table:
    
    [dependency-groups]
    group-a = ["foo"]
    group-b = ["foo>1.0"]
    group-c = ["foo<1.0"]
    all = [
        "foo",
        {include-group = "group-a"},
        {include-group = "group-b"},
        {include-group = "group-c"},
    ]
    

The resolved value of `all` SHOULD be `["foo", "foo", "foo>1.0", "foo<1.0"]`. Tools should handle such a list exactly as they would handle any other case in which they are asked to process the same requirement multiple times with different version constraints.

Dependency Group Includes may include groups containing Dependency Group Includes, in which case those includes should be expanded as well. Dependency Group Includes MUST NOT include cycles, and tools SHOULD report an error if they detect a cycle.

### Package Building¶

Build backends MUST NOT include Dependency Group data in built distributions as package metadata. This means that sdist `PKG-INFO` and wheel `METADATA` files should not include referenceable fields containing dependency groups.

It is, however, valid to use dependency groups in the evaluation of dynamic metadata, and `pyproject.toml` files included in sdists will still contain `[dependency-groups]`. However, the table’s contents are not part of a built package’s interfaces.

### Installing Dependency Groups & Extras¶

There is no syntax or specification-defined interface for installing or referring to dependency groups. Tools are expected to provide dedicated interfaces for this purpose.

## Serve Distribution Metadata in the Simple Repository API¶

In a simple repository’s project page, each anchor tag pointing to a distribution MAY have a `data-dist-info-metadata` attribute. The presence of the attribute indicates the distribution represented by the anchor tag MUST contain a Core Metadata file that will not be modified when the distribution is processed and/or installed.

If a `data-dist-info-metadata` attribute is present, the repository MUST serve the distribution’s Core Metadata file alongside the distribution with a `.metadata` appended to the distribution’s file name. For example, the Core Metadata of a distribution served at `/files/distribution-1.0-py3.none.any.whl` would be located at `/files/distribution-1.0-py3.none.any.whl.metadata`. This is similar to how the base HTML API specification specifies the GPG signature file’s location.

The repository SHOULD provide the hash of the Core Metadata file as the `data-dist-info-metadata` attribute’s value using the syntax `<hashname>=<hashvalue>`, where `<hashname>` is the lower cased name of the hash function used, and `<hashvalue>` is the hex encoded digest. The repository MAY use `true` as the attribute’s value if a hash is unavailable.

### Backwards Compatibility¶

If an anchor tag lacks the `data-dist-info-metadata` attribute, tools are expected to revert to their current behaviour of downloading the distribution to inspect the metadata.

Older tools not supporting the new `data-dist-info-metadata` attribute are expected to ignore the attribute and maintain their current behaviour of downloading the distribution to inspect the metadata. This is similar to how prior `data-` attribute additions expect existing tools to operate.

## JSON-based Simple API for Python Package Indexes¶

To enable response parsing with only the standard library, this spec specifies that all responses (besides the files themselves, and the HTML responses from the base HTML API specification) should be serialized using JSON.

To enable zero configuration discovery and to minimize the amount of additional HTTP requests, this spec extends the base HTML API specification such that all of the API endpoints (other than the files themselves) will utilize HTTP content negotiation to allow client and server to select the correct serialization format to serve, i.e. either HTML or JSON.

  * `versions`: A list of version strings specifying all of the project versions uploaded for this project. The value of `versions` is logically a set, and as such may not contain duplicates, and the order of the versions is not significant.

Note

All of the files listed in the `files` key MUST be associated with one of the versions in the `versions` key. The `versions` key MAY contain versions with no associated files (to represent versions with no files uploaded, if the server has such a concept).

Note

Because servers may hold “legacy” data from before the adoption of the version specifiers specification (VSS), version strings currently cannot be required to be valid VSS versions, and therefore cannot be assumed to be orderable using the VSS rules. However, servers SHOULD use normalized VSS versions where possible.

Note

The `versions` key was added with API version 1.1.

Each individual file dictionary has the following keys:

  * `filename`: The filename that is being represented.

  * `url`: The URL that the file can be fetched from.

  * `hashes`: A dictionary mapping a hash name to a hex encoded digest of the file. Multiple hashes can be included, and it is up to the client to decide what to do with multiple hashes (it may validate all of them or a subset of them, or nothing at all). These hash names SHOULD always be normalized to be lowercase.

The `hashes` dictionary MUST be present, even if no hashes are available for the file, however it is HIGHLY recommended that at least one secure, guaranteed-to-be-available hash is always included.

By default, any hash algorithm available via `hashlib` (specifically any that can be passed to `hashlib.new()` and do not require additional parameters) can be used as a key for the hashes dictionary. At least one secure algorithm from `hashlib.algorithms_guaranteed` SHOULD always be included. At the time of this spec, `sha256` specifically is recommended.

  * `requires-python`: An optional key that exposes the Requires-Python metadata field. Where this is present, installer tools SHOULD ignore the download when installing to a Python version that doesn’t satisfy the requirement.

Unlike `data-requires-python` in the base HTML API specification, the `requires-python` key does not require any special escaping other than anything JSON does naturally.

  * `core-metadata`: An optional key that indicates that metadata for this file is available, via the same location as specified in the API metadata file specification (`{file_url}.metadata`). Where this is present, it MUST be either a boolean to indicate if the file has an associated metadata file, or a dictionary mapping hash names to a hex encoded digest of the metadata’s hash.

When this is a dictionary of hashes instead of a boolean, then all the same requirements and recommendations as the `hashes` key hold true for this key as well.

If this key is missing then the metadata file may or may not exist. If the key value is truthy, then the metadata file is present, and if it is falsey then it is not.

It is recommended that servers make the hashes of the metadata file available if possible.

  * `dist-info-metadata`: An optional, deprecated alias for `core-metadata`.

Index clients MAY consume this key if present, as a legacy fallback for `core-metadata`.

Important

`dist-info-metadata` was standardized with PEP 658 and renamed to `core-metadata` with PEP 714.

  * `gpg-sig`: An optional key that acts a boolean to indicate if the file has an associated GPG signature or not. The URL for the signature file follows what is specified in the base HTML API specification (`{file_url}.asc`). If this key does not exist, then the signature may or may not exist.

  * `yanked`: An optional key which may be either a boolean to indicate if the file has been yanked, or a non empty, but otherwise arbitrary, string to indicate that a file has been yanked with a specific reason. If the `yanked` key is present and is a truthy value, then it SHOULD be interpreted as indicating that the file pointed to by the `url` field has been “Yanked”.

Note

The semantics of how tools should handle yanked files is described in File Yanking.

  * `size`: A mandatory key. It MUST contain an integer which is the file size in bytes.

Note

The `size` key was added with API version 1.1.

  * `upload-time`: An optional key that, if present, MUST contain a valid ISO 8601 date/time string in the format `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.ffffffZ` which represents the time the file was uploaded to the index.

As indicated by the `Z` suffix, the upload time MUST use the UTC timezone. The fractional seconds part of the timestamp (the `.ffffff` part) is optional, and if present may contain up to 6 digits of precision. If a server does not record upload time information for a file, it MAY omit the `upload-time` key.

Note

The `upload-time` key was added with API version 1.1.

  * `provenance`: An optional key which, if present MUST be either a JSON string or `null`. If not `null`, it MUST be a URL to the file’s associated provenance, with the same rules as `data-provenance` in the base HTML API specification.

Note

The `provenance` field was added with API version 1.3.

As an example:
    
    {
      "meta": {
        "api-version": "1.4",
        "project-status": "active",
        "project-status-reason": "this project is not yet haunted"
      },
      "name": "holygrail",
      "files": [
        {
          "filename": "holygrail-1.0.tar.gz",
          "url": "https://example.com/files/holygrail-1.0.tar.gz",
          "hashes": {"sha256": "...", "blake2b": "..."},
          "requires-python": ">=3.7",
          "yanked": "Had a vulnerability",
          "size": 123456
        },
        {
          "filename": "holygrail-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
          "url": "https://example.com/files/holygrail-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
          "hashes": {"sha256": "...", "blake2b": "..."},
          "requires-python": ">=3.7",
          "dist-info-metadata": true,
          "provenance": "https://example.com/files/holygrail-1.0-py3-none-any.whl.provenance",
          "size": 1337
        }
      ],
      "versions": ["1.0"]
    }
    

Note

While the `files` key is an array, and thus is required to be in some kind of an order, neither the base HTML API specification nor this spec requires any specific ordering nor that the ordering is consistent from one request to the next. Mentally this is best thought of as a set, but both JSON and HTML lack the functionality to have sets.

## History¶

  * September 2015: initial form of the HTML format, in PEP 503

  * July 2016: Requires-Python metadata, in an update to PEP 503

  * May 2019: “yank” support, in PEP 592

  * July 2020: API versioning convention and metadata, and declaring the HTML format as API v1, in PEP 629

  * May 2021: providing package metadata independently from a package, in PEP 658

  * May 2022: initial form of the JSON format, with a mechanism for clients to choose between them, and declaring both formats as API v1, in PEP 691

  * October 2022: project versions and file size and upload-time in the JSON format, in PEP 700

  * June 2023: renaming the field which provides package metadata independently from a package, in PEP 714

  * November 2024: provenance metadata in the HTML and JSON formats, in PEP 740

  * July 2025: project status markers in the HTML and JSON formats, in PEP 792

  * July 2025: layout changes (dedicated page for file yanking, introduce concepts before API details)

  * June 2026: PEP 833 formally “freezes” the HTML representation of the simple API--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Specification¶

Links in the simple repository MAY have a `data-yanked` attribute which may have no value, or may have an arbitrary string as a value. The presence of a `data-yanked` attribute SHOULD be interpreted as indicating that the file pointed to by this particular link has been “Yanked”, and should not generally be selected by an installer, except under specific scenarios.

The value of the `data-yanked` attribute, if present, is an arbitrary string that represents the reason for why the file has been yanked. Tools that process the simple repository API MAY surface this string to end users.

The yanked attribute is not immutable once set, and may be rescinded in the future (and once rescinded, may be reset as well). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership

Status: Proposed

This proposal revises ADR 11's selector promotion and default-tag coupling when implemented. ADR 11 remains the current decision; it is not superseded by this documentation change.

## Context

The owner selected Rust/Cargo, npm/pnpm and Python/PyPI as the current scope, with architectural room for Go and .NET/NuGet. The system audit found that display promotion leaks into dependency rewrites, historical ownership and shared tag/forge ordering. Fresh Cargo/Maturin projects also fail because one package requires one grammar. Evidence and implementation work are recorded in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

## Proposed decision

- Use canonical slash-qualified distribution references for new exact inputs, authored and generated data; reject new bare and colon-form aliases. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem.
- Separate release ownership, distribution identity, authoritative version source and external effects. Reuse existing types and graphs; do not add a general plugin framework or opaque IDs without need.
- Read existing bare/colon references only through a deliberate compatibility/migration boundary with established ownership. Preserve historical tag ownership without using display promotion as a release-identity change.
- Keep native names and manifest context for dependency edits, inherited/derived versions and publisher arguments.
- Within Callisto's release-operation graph, shared external effects have one owner and wait for every required publication/output of that owner. For current ecosystems, public announcement follows registry completion; a future Go source tag can itself be publication.
- Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject hooks; effects initiated by owner-defined hooks are outside Callisto's release-operation graph.
- Reruns observe every required effect, including unfinished work after tag creation and missing Python files. Keep ADR 2's committed roster and ADR 3's no-journal recovery.

The exact owner representation, legacy-record migration, wire schema migration and channel/private-registry policies must be resolved in the relevant implementation change. This ADR does not approve those unspecified details or introduce release gates.

## Options considered

- Keep collision-triggered bare/qualified identity everywhere: retains inference rules at every new consumer and lets unrelated workspace changes alter identity behavior.
- Canonicalize one package ID but retain one grammar and per-distribution completion: does not represent Maturin version authority or shared tag/forge effects.
- Introduce a universal graph/plugin/build system: exceeds the supported use cases and duplicates ecosystem tools.

## Consequences

Pre-v1 breaking references are allowed by the owner requirement, but historical releases and committed decisions still need explicit compatibility. Cargo/npm/Python outputs can share an owner without pretending their native versions or registry evidence are interchangeable. Go/NuGet remain design examples, not shipped adapters.

## Sources

- Owner scope and canonical-identity discussion, 2026-09-26; [REQ-DX-V1](../specs/REQ-DX-V1.md).
- [Scoped model and primary-source prior art](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).
- [System findings and verification limits](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).

# 11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history

Status: Accepted (implemented in #167)

## Context

- A package's id was its primary manifest name. When a second directory declared the same name in another ecosystem, walking promoted both to `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`).
- Everything derived from the id changed with it. The default tag template was `{id}@{version}`, so an existing Cargo `foo` looked for `cargo/foo@*` tags, lost `foo@1.0.0`, and planned its next release from no prior tag.
- Selectors already tolerate promotion: `cargo/foo` resolves whether or not the package is promoted.

## Decision

- A package's stable identity is its workspace-relative directory: `Package::key() -> Option<PackageKey>` in `crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs`.
- `PackageId` is the display and selector form. Promotion changes how it prints (`foo` becomes `cargo/foo`), which bare selectors are ambiguous (E103), and the namespace of newly created default tags. The directory key and CHANGELOG path do not change.
- History recorded under a bare name follows the package that owned the name. Default tags are `{display id}@{version}` (`foo@1.0.0`, then `cargo/foo@1.1.0` once promoted), and a promoted package also finds `foo@*` tags whose commit contains its own manifest and no same-named package's. A bare `pre.json` key moves to the one same-named package that existed when `pre.json` was added. The CHANGELOG path comes from the directory.
- No configuration is needed. E101 is raised only when an explicit `tag-template` equals another package's default; E245 only when a bare `pre.json` key has no single owner.

## Options considered

- **Primary manifest name as key** — rejected: promotion changed the id, and with it the tag lookup of an already-released package.
- **Re-key every in-run map by `PackageKey`** — rejected for now: about 66 maps over roughly 1,000 `PackageId` uses. Promotion is computed once per walk, so within a run `PackageId` maps one-to-one onto `PackageKey`; re-keying would change no behavior.
- **Default tags from the native name (`foo@{version}`) for every package** — rejected: promoted `cargo/foo` and `npm/foo` would share tags, so one of them needed a `tag-template` (E101), and already-promoted workspaces would change their tag names.
- **Fall back to `{name}@` tags without an ownership check** — rejected: the newly added package would adopt the old one's releases.

## Consequences

- Adding a same-named package changes new default tag names, but does not rename existing tags or move the CHANGELOG. Historical bare tags and pre-release baselines are assigned through the ownership fallback; rename, manifest-roster and demotion gaps are tracked in [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).
- Workspaces that are already promoted keep their `cargo/foo@*` tags unchanged.
- Ownership costs one `git rev-parse` per candidate tag of a promoted package.
- A pending changeset that names the bare `foo` is ambiguous after promotion (E103, WS-ID-06) and must be qualified.

## Enforcement

- `TagTemplate::default_for` in `crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs`; the ownership fallback in `TagIndex::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/tags.rs`); `assign_promoted_pre_keys` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`.
- `promotion_changes_the_display_id_but_not_the_key` in `crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`; `crates/callisto-cli/tests/identity_promotion_tests.rs`.
- WS-ID-03 and WS-ID-08 in `docs/specs/workspace.json`.

## Revisit when

- Something persists a package reference that is not a selector, tag or path, such as a cache keyed by package. It should use `PackageKey`.
- A package can move directories while keeping its identity.

## Sources

- Owner decision, `docs/projects/ROAD-TO-V1.md` "v1 fix plan" decisions (2026-09-25)
- #167 ("refactor(identity)!: key packages by directory; promotion is display-only") and its zero-config follow-up
